honors.title: 2012 Theodore Cohn Memorial Scholarship Recipient
honors.description:
Professor Theodore Cohn was a professor of Bioengineering and Vision Science at the University of California, Berkeley. In his 36 years on the UC Berkeley faculty, Professor Cohn was a leading researcher in signal detection theory and its real-world applications; and his research spanned many fields. From studying how people pick signals out of cluttered backgrounds, to elucidating neural responses to visual input, to applying that knowledge to design improved traffic safety devices, his work was united by the common theme of vision. Professor Cohn was widely respected for his research and equally admired for his service to UC Berkeley and his dedication to his students and colleagues. He was strongly committed to mentoring students from disadvantaged backgrounds or any student seeking to discover his or her academic passion.

After his passing, Professor Cohn's family established this scholarship award in order to select and recognize one undergraduate student each year for their achievements and success in their research.

honors.title: 2012 URAP Summer Research Fellowship
honors.description: Summer research fellowship through the Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program (URAP) at the Levi Lab in the UC Berkeley School of Optometry. Research investigated therapeutic applications of software to regain neural plasticity for the treatment of amblyopia.
honors.issuer: Issued by URAP (Undergraduate Research Apprentice Program) · Mar 2012
